chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, by an unbroken chain, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to a man: 'What is considered to be the young one (al-fata) among you?' He said to him, 'The youth.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'No! The young one (al-fata) is the Believer. Indeed, the Companions of the Cave were old men, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, called them young men (fityah) due to their belief.'

key_terms.الشَّابُّ: The youth / young man (referring to age)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual meaning of 'al-fata' (youth) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that 'al-fata' denotes spiritual maturity and steadfastness in faith rather than chronological youth, citing the Companions of the Cave as exemplars who were termed 'fityah' due to their vigorous conviction despite their age. This interpretation aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition where 'fityah' signifies those who possess the vitality of belief and readiness for sacrifice, transcending physical attributes. The hadith underscores the theological principle that true youthhood is measured by the strength of one's Iman and adherence to truth.

en.hubeali: H 15042 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, by an unbroken chain, said:

‘Abu Abdullahasws said to a man: ‘What are considered to be the young ones (Al-Fati) among you?’ He said to himasws, ‘The youth’. So heasws said; ‘No! Al-Fati is the Believer. The Companions of the Cave (As’haab Al-Kahf) were old people, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Called them ‘Young men’ due to their belief’.
en.sarwar: Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Sadeyr who said: ‘A man asked Abu Ja’far (a.s.) about the Statement of Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic: “[34:19] And they said: O our Lord! make spaces to be longer between our journeys; and they were unjust to themselves”. He (a.s.) said: ‘They were a people who live in two inter-connected villages and were able to see each other, and rivers which flowed, and phenomenal wealth. They denied the Favours of Allah (azwj) and changed what was in themselves, so Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic Sent the flood of Al-Aram against them. Their two villages were submerged, and their houses were spoilt, and their wealth was gone. It changed their plantations into two plantations to be only with the edible plants of bitter tamarisk (a troublesome weed) and a few Lutus trees. Then Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic Said: “[34:17] This We requited them with because they disbelieved; and We do not punish any but the ungrateful”.
